The '''65th Academy Awards''' ceremony, presented by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored [[1992 in film|films released in 1992]] in the United States and took place on March 29, 1993, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in Los Angeles beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented Academy Awards (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Gilbert Cates|Gil Cates]] and directed by [[Jeff Margolis]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Marx |first=Andy |title=4th Oscarcast for Cates |url=https://variety.com/1992/film/awards/4th-oscarcast-for-cates-100501/ |access-date=February 19, 2014 |work=Variety |date=November 11, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306132553/http://variety.com/1992/film/awards/4th-oscarcast-for-cates-100501/ |archive-date=March 6, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=418}}</ref> Actor [[Billy Crystal]] hosted the show for the fourth consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news|last=MacMinn |first=Aleene |title=Morning Report: Movies |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-02-10-ca-1151-story.html |access-date=February 19, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times  |date=February 10, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140912123121/http://articles.latimes.com/1993-02-10/entertainment/ca-1151_1_major-movie |archive-date=September 12, 2014 }}</ref> In related events, during a ceremony held at the [[Century Plaza Hotel]] in Los Angeles on March 6, the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by host [[Sharon Stone]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|access-date=July 31, 2013|publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Unforgiven]]'' won four Oscars, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Fox |first=David J. |title='Unforgiven' Top Film; Pacino, Thompson Win : Academy Awards: Eastwood named best director. Oscars for supporting roles go to Hackman and Tomei. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-03-30-mn-16785-story.html |access-date=February 25, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 31, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307234002/http://articles.latimes.com/1993-03-30/news/mn-16785_1_film-academy |archive-date=March 7, 2014 }}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992 film)|Bram Stoker's Dracula]]'' and ''[[Howards End (film)|Howards End]]'' with three awards, ''[[Aladdin (1992 Disney film)|Aladdin]]'' with two, and ''[[The Crying Game]]'', ''[[Death Becomes Her]]'', ''[[Educating Peter]]'', ''[[Indochine (film)|Indochine]]'', ''[[The Last of the Mohicans (1992 film)|The Last of the Mohicans]]'', ''[[Mona Lisa Descending a Staircase]]'', ''[[My Cousin Vinny]]'', ''[[Omnibus (film)|Omnibus]]'', ''[[The Panama Deception]]'', ''[[A River Runs Through It (film)|A River Runs Through It]]'', and ''[[Scent of a Woman (1992 film)|Scent of a Woman]]'' with one. The telecast garnered 45.7 million viewers in the United States.<ref name="Glamour Bowl">{{cite news|last=Johnson |first=Greg |title=Call It the Glamour Bowl |url=https://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/18/business/fi-18458/2 |access-date=August 26, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 18, 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928053918/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/18/business/fi-18458/2 |archive-date=September 28, 2013 }}</ref>

==Winners and nominees==
The nominees for the 65th Academy Awards were announced on February 17, 1993, at the [[Samuel Goldwyn Theater]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], by [[Robert Rehme]], president of the academy, and actress [[Mercedes Ruehl]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Weinraub |first=Bernard |title=3 Films Dominate Nominees in Oscar Contest |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/02/18/movies/3-films-dominate-nominees-in-oscar-contest.html |access-date=February 19, 2014 |work=The New York Times  |date=February 18, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312082840/http://www.nytimes.com/1993/02/18/movies/3-films-dominate-nominees-in-oscar-contest.html |archive-date=March 12, 2014 }}</ref> ''[[Howards End (film)|Howards End]]'' and ''[[Unforgiven]]'' led all nominees with nine nominations each.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fox |first=David J. |title=The 65th Academy Award Nominations: The Declaration of Independents : The nominations: 'Howards End' and 'Unforgiven' get nine apiece, 'The Crying Game' six. Non-studio and maverick filmmakers have a field day. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-02-18-ca-463-story.html |access-date=February 18, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=February 18, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105224502/http://articles.latimes.com/1993-02-18/entertainment/ca-463_1_howards-end |archive-date=November 5, 2012 }}</ref>

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 29, 1993. Best Director winner [[Clint Eastwood]] became the seventh person nominated for lead acting and directing for the same film.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Ebert|first1=Roger|title=Oscars Honor Period Pieces But 'Player,' 'Malcolm X' Passed Over|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|publisher=Tim Knight|date=February 18, 1993|page=37}}</ref> Best Actor winner [[Al Pacino]] was the sixth performer to receive [[List of actors nominated for multiple Academy Awards in the same year|nominations in the lead and supporting categories in the same year]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Rea |first=Steven |title=In Line For Oscars "Howards End" And Clint Eastwood's "Unforgiven" Got Nine Academy Award Nominations Each. And Makers Of "The Crying Game" May Get The Last Laugh, With Six Shots at the Statuette. |url=http://articles.philly.com/1993-02-18/entertainment/25955125_1_academy-award-nominations-unforgiven-mary-mcdonnell |access-date=February 25, 2014 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |publisher=H.F. Gerry Lenfest |date=February 18, 1993 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306045014/http://articles.philly.com/1993-02-18/entertainment/25955125_1_academy-award-nominations-unforgiven-mary-mcdonnell |archive-date=March 6, 2014 }}</ref> He also became the first person to win in the lead acting category after achieving the aforementioned feat.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1173}}</ref> By virtue of his second straight win in both music categories, [[Alan Menken]] became the third person to win two Oscars in two consecutive years.<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=424}}</ref>

===Honorary Award===

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Billy Crystal VF 2012 Shankbone.JPG|thumb|right|[[Billy Crystal]] hosted the 65th Academy Awards.|alt=Photo of Billy Crystal at the 2012 Tribeca Film Festival.]]

After the success of the [[64th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]] which won several [[Emmy]]s and critical acclaim, the academy rehired producer [[Gil Cates]] for the fourth consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cates to Repeat As Oscars Producer|work=San Francisco Chronicle|date=November 13, 1992|page=C2}}</ref> In February 1993, actor and comedian [[Billy Crystal]] was chosen by Cates as host also for the fourth straight time.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Williams|first1=Jeannie|title=Bily Crystal, back as Mr. Oscar night|work=USA Today|date=February 5, 1993|page=2D}}</ref> Cates justified the decision to hire him saying, "He is a major movie star with a talent for moving the evening's entertainment along."<ref>{{cite news|title='Perfect host' appointed|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|publisher=Phillip Crawley|date=February 6, 1993|page=C6}}</ref> According to an article by [[Army Archerd]] published in ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', Crystal initially declined to host again citing his busy film schedule that included ''[[Mr. Saturday Night]]'' and ''[[City Slickers II: The Legend of Curly's Gold]]''.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Williams|first1=Jeannie|title=Roping Crystal into Oscar duty|work=USA Today|date=February 18, 1993|page=2D}}</ref> However, after Cates sent him a funeral wreath with a poem declaring "The show and I are dead without you" followed by a head of a fake dead horse similar to one featured in the film ''[[The Godfather]]'', Crystal accepted the role as emcee.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Archerd |first1=Army |title=Cates 'convinces' Crystal to m.c. Oscars again |url=https://variety.com/1993/voices/columns/cates-convinces-crystal-to-m-c-oscars-again-1117862127/ |access-date=June 20, 2014 |work=Variety  |date=February 16, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150112143742/http://variety.com/1993/voices/columns/cates-convinces-crystal-to-m-c-oscars-again-1117862127/ |archive-date=January 12, 2015 }}</ref>

As with previous ceremonies he produced, Cates centered the show around a theme. Inspired by the [[Year of the Woman]] in which a record four women were elected to the [[United States Senate]], Cates christened the 1993 show with the theme "Oscar Celebrates Women and the Movies".<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=872}}</ref> In tandem with the theme, AMPAS gathered 67 female Oscar winners of every category for a photo that was later shown at the start of the telecast.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=875}}</ref> Actress and singer [[Liza Minnelli]] performed "Ladies' Day", a song written by [[Fred Ebb]] and [[John Kander]] specifically for the broadcast.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=886}}</ref> Oscar-winning documentarian [[Lynne Littman]] assembled a montage highlighting women in film.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=880}}</ref>

Several other people participated in the production of the ceremony. [[Bill Conti]] served as conductor and musical supervisor for the ceremony.<ref>{{cite news|title=Oscar watch |url=https://variety.com/1993/film/news/oscar-watch-7-102639/ |access-date=June 20, 2014 |work=Variety  |date=January 5, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119034216/http://variety.com/1993/film/news/oscar-watch-7-102639/ |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref> Choreographer [[Debbie Allen]] supervised the Best Song nominee performances and the "Ladies' Night" musical number.<ref>{{cite news|title=Oscar Dance Tryouts Sunday |url=https://variety.com/1993/film/news/oscar-dance-tryouts-sunday-104202/ |access-date=June 20, 2014 |work=Variety  |date=February 22, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119024729/http://variety.com/1993/film/news/oscar-dance-tryouts-sunday-104202/ |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref> Voice actress Randy Thomas served as announcer of the telecast becoming the first woman to do so.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=879}}</ref>

[[Richard Gere]] became the source of some controversy when, before presenting Best Art Direction, began an impromptu speech criticizing the [[Human rights in China|status of human rights in China]] and directly addressed then-leader of China [[Deng Xiaoping]], calling on him to grant independence to [[Tibet]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Louison |first=Cole |date=2007-04-12 |title=Richard Gere: The Lost Transcript |url=https://www.gq.com/story/richard-gere-oscar-academy-awards-transcript-dalai-llama |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=GQ |language=en-US}}</ref> Gere’s speech was met with applause from the audience but producer [[Gilbert Cates|Gil Cates]] banned the actor from presenting at the ceremony for 20 years.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Was Richard Gere really banned from the Oscars for 20 years? It's complicated |url=https://ew.com/was-richard-gere-really-banned-from-the-oscars-for-20-years-11865631 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20251210003347/https://ew.com/was-richard-gere-really-banned-from-the-oscars-for-20-years-11865631 |archive-date=2025-12-10 |access-date=2026-09-16 |work=EW.com |language=en}}</ref> The Chinese government banned Gere from entering China for life.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1997-11-10 |title=Can You Go Home Again? |url=https://www.newsweek.com/can-you-go-home-again-171048 |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref>

At the time of the nominations announcement on February 17, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $252 million, with an average of $50.4 million per film.<ref name="BoxOfficeMojoOscars" /> ''A Few Good Men'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $120 million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by ''Unforgiven'' ($75.2 million), ''Scent of a Woman'' ($34.1 million), ''The Crying Game'' ($14 million), and finally ''Howards End'' ($8.7 million).<ref name="BoxOfficeMojoOscars" />

Of the top 50 grossing movies of the year, 38 nominations went to 13 films on the list. Only ''A Few Good Men'' (6th), ''Unforgiven'' (17th), ''Malcolm X'' (30th) and ''Scent of a Woman'' (38th) were nominated for directing, acting, screenwriting, or Best Picture.<ref name="boxofficemojooscars">{{cite web|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1993-0216&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1992&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |title=1992 Domestic Grosses |publisher=Box Office Mojo |access-date=February 25, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119042438/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1993-0216&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1992&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref> The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were ''Aladdin'' (1st), ''Batman Returns'' (3rd), ''Basic Instinct'' (8th), ''The Bodyguard'' (9th), ''Under Siege'' (12th), ''Bram Stoker's Dracula'' (14th), ''The Last of the Mohicans'' (16th), ''Death Becomes Her'' (22nd), and ''Alien<sup>3</sup>'' (26th).<ref name="boxofficemojooscars" />

===Critical reviews and ratings===
The show received a negative reception from most media publications. Associated Press television critic [[Frazier Moore]] lamented that Crystal "seemed incredibly listless". He also questioned the purpose of the "Year of the Woman" theme writing, "The Oscar show itself seemed at odds with its own feminist theme."<ref>{{cite news|last=Moore|first=Frazier|title=Billy Crystal's Performance Lame|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1957&dat=19930330&id=Bg0xAAAAIBAJ&sjid=IOEFAAAAIBAJ&pg=3345,7229336|access-date=February 26, 2014|work=[[The Daily Gazette]]|date=March 30, 1993|archive-date=February 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205083758/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1957&dat=19930330&id=Bg0xAAAAIBAJ&sjid=IOEFAAAAIBAJ&pg=3345,7229336|url-status=live}}</ref> Robert Bianco from the ''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'' derided Allen's musical production numbers, comparing them to the disastrous opening number at the [[61st Academy Awards|61st ceremony]] held in 1989.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bianco|first=Robert|title=Crystal Can't Save Disastrous Oscars Show|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=19930330&id=xNdRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Sm4DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6977,6838257|access-date=February 26, 2014|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=March 30, 1993|archive-date=February 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205083653/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=19930330&id=xNdRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Sm4DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6977,6838257|url-status=live}}</ref> Columnist Matt Roush of ''[[USA Today]]'' complained, "Crystal, in a by-now-familiar performance, has, in four years, taken a plum assignment and, by repetition, reduced it to shtick." He also wrote that, "The song medley is getting old hat," and the "smug references to his flop ''[[Mr. Saturday Night]]'' were out of an improv amateur night."<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=892}}</ref>

The telecast also received unfavorable reaction from various public feminist figures. In an interview with ''[[Los Angeles Daily News]]'', author and activist [[Betty Friedan]] condemned the "Year of the Woman" theme, commenting, "It had no basis in reality. On behalf of women directors, cinematographer, and producers, I resent the travesty of calling that a tribute."<ref name="feminine">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=893}}</ref> Likewise, President of the [[National Organization for Women]]'s Los Angeles chapter [[Tammy Bruce]] chastised ceremony's feminist tribute as "one of the most hypocritical, patronizing things I saw in my whole life."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Karlak|first1=Pat|last2=Swertlow|first2=Frank|title=Hollywood's Hollow Salute Oscars' 'Year of Woman' Patronizing, Many Say|work=[[The Plain Dealer]]|page=3C}}</ref> In response, Gil Cates responded towards the criticism of the theme stating, "The theme developed and raised consciousness in a way that I think is positive, not only for the individual in general but for individual women specifically."<ref name="feminine" /> He also quoted an ancient Chinese proverb later made famous by former [[First Lady of the United States|U.S. First Lady]] [[Eleanor Roosevelt]] saying, "[[Better to light a candle than curse the darkness|It is better to light one candle than to curse the darkness]]."<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=313}}</ref>

Despite the adverse reception, the ABC broadcast drew in an average of 45.7 million people over its length, which was a 3% increase from the [[64th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref name="Glamour Bowl"/> The show also drew higher [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony with 31.2% of households watching over a 51 share.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schwed |first1=Mark |url=https://variety.com/1993/tv/news/kudocast-s-nielsen-ratings-highest-in-10-years-105508/ |access-date=August 8, 2015 |work=Variety  |title=Kudocast's Nielsen ratings highest in 10 years |date=March 30, 1993 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119050617/http://variety.com/1993/tv/news/kudocast-s-nielsen-ratings-highest-in-10-years-105508/ |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Carter |first1=Bill |title=TV Notes;Oscar Numbers Slip |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/03/27/movies/tv-notes-oscar-numbers-slip.html |access-date=October 15, 2015 |work=The New York Times  |date=March 27, 1996 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119074457/http://www.nytimes.com/1996/03/27/movies/tv-notes-oscar-numbers-slip.html |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }}</ref> It also drew a higher 18–49 demo rating with a 20.1 rating among viewers in that demographic.<ref name="TVB Oscars">{{cite news|title=Academy Awards ratings |publisher=[[Television Bureau of Advertising]] |url=http://www.tvb.org/media/file/Academy_Awards.pdf |access-date=June 27, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515152338/http://www.tvb.org/media/file/Academy_Awards.pdf |archive-date=May 15, 2013 }}</ref>

:'''A'''{{note|Uruguay}}: The Academy revoked the Best Foreign Language Film nomination of [[List of Uruguayan submissions for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Uruguay]]'s ''[[A Place in the World (film)|A Place in the World]]'' after an investigation that determined the film as an [[Cinema of Argentina|Argentine production]] and therefore violated the Academy's rules which require that there be "substantial filmmaking input from the country that submits the film".<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=873}}</ref>

:'''B'''{{note|Hepburn}}: Hepburn's son [[Sean Hepburn Ferrer]] accepted the award at the ceremony on her behalf.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rickey |first1=Carrie |title=In Like Clint Oscar's Tribute Was Fitting, Given That Women Garnered A Surprising Share of Awards. (for Al Pacino, The Magic Even Trickled Down to the Title "Scent of a Woman".) |url=http://articles.philly.com/1993-03-30/entertainment/25952012_1_ian-whittaker-actor-statuette-oscars |access-date=June 20, 2014 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |publisher=H.F. Gerry Lenfest |date=March 30, 1993 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914085601/http://articles.philly.com/1993-03-30/entertainment/25952012_1_ian-whittaker-actor-statuette-oscars |archive-date=September 14, 2015 }}</ref>
